# Psalms of Solomon — Psalm 4 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Greek MS (Codex Vindobonensis) | **Section:** Against the Hypocrite Who Sits in the Council

---

**4:1** Why dost thou sit in the council of the devout, O profaner,
when thy heart is far from the LORD,

**4:2** provoking by transgressions the God of Israel,
excess in the lawless deeds of transgressors?

**4:3** Reckless in speech, reckless in appearance beyond all [others];
he is harsh in [his] words to reprove sinners.

**4:4** His hand is [raised] first against him as if with zeal,
and yet he himself is guilty concerning many sins of passion.

**4:5** His eyes are [upon] every woman without distinction;
his tongue lies when he makes a covenant with [false] oath.

**4:6** In the night and in secret he sins;
he is a thief, and his appearance is pure.

**4:7** His eyes are upon every woman;
his tongue lies when he makes a [false] treaty.

**4:8** May God remove those who live in hypocrisy
from among the devout,
their life [wasted] with the flesh of an alien.

**4:9** May God destroy those who live in hypocrisy
with corruption, because their life is dishonest.

**4:10** God, expose his deeds to ridicule before all Israel;
expose them as he has done to others.

**4:11** May his portion be poverty and want;
may his inheritance be empty.

**4:12** His old age in childlessness,
and let him die in desolation.

**4:13** May the bones of the slanderers be scattered far from those who fear the LORD;
may there be no sleep for them in their resting-place in distress.

**4:14** For with his tongue he deceives honorable men;
he leads astray the souls of the simple with lawless words.

**4:15** He cuts short the life of the young man;
he destroys the beauty of the young woman.

**4:16** He causes the noble to stumble in hidden ways,
before the eyes of all.

**4:17** May he be homeless and wandering;
may no one dwell in his house.

**4:18** May his days on earth be few;
may his old age be in shame and poverty.

**4:19** May the LORD smite those who sit on their throne,
and rule the simple among the devout.

**4:20** Their dwelling place may God destroy in desolation;
may he take away their seed from the earth.

**4:21** Because with deceit they beguiled the souls of the pious,
and they led astray the house of Israel.

**4:22** For this reason, Lord, grant them their recompense
by handing them over to the hands of the devout.

**4:23** Spare me, O God, from the sinner
who devises evil against me.

**4:24** Far from me keep the evil one, O LORD;
let his face be put to shame before me.

**4:25** Guide my steps, O LORD, in thy truth,
and let not the sins of the wicked overcome me.

---

*EMET notes: Translated from the Greek (Codex Vindobonensis). Hyphenated compounds preserve construct chains. Bracketed words [thus] are implied by grammar but absent from the surface text.*
